recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Potato-Mushroom Gratin and Tomato-Basil Relish
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. A rectangular portion of golden-brown potato-mushroom gratin, showcasing distinct layers and a crispy top, anchors one side. Adjacent is a whole, pan-seared chicken breast, its skin deeply golden and caramelized, subtly glistening. A vibrant mound of freshly prepared tomato-basil relish, with diced red tomatoes and bright green basil leaves, is spooned artfully over the chicken, adding a pop of contrasting color. A single fresh basil leaf garnishes the relish. Colors are natural: golden-brown chicken and gratin, deep red tomatoes, vivid green basil. Moderate negative space ensures a professional yet approachable presentation. The background features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and subtly blurred restaurant elements, conveying a casual bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Ripe cherry tomatoes or small Roma tomatoes
Red wine vinegar or balsamic glaze

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Thinly slice potatoes (1-2mm thick) using a mandoline or sharp knife. Slice mushrooms. Mince 2 cloves garlic and chop onion/shallots.

In a large pan, melt 15g butter over medium heat. Sauté onion/shallots until softened, about 3 minutes. Add mushrooms and remaining minced garlic. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Layer half the sliced potatoes in a greased 20x20 cm baking dish. Top with half the mushroom mixture. Repeat layers.
Whisk heavy cream with chicken broth, salt, and pepper. Pour over potato layers. Sprinkle with half the Parmesan cheese.

Bake for 30 minutes, covered. Uncover, sprinkle with remaining Parmesan, and bake for another 20-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown. Let rest 5 minutes before cutting into portions.
Dice cherry or Roma tomatoes into small cubes. Finely chop fresh basil leaves. Mince 2 cloves garlic.
In a small bowl, combine diced tomatoes, chopped basil, minced garlic, 30ml olive oil, and red wine vinegar/balsamic glaze. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken breasts to hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Place a portion of potato-mushroom gratin on each plate. Arrange a pan-seared chicken breast beside it. Spoon tomato-basil relish over the chicken. Garnish with a fresh basil leaf.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chicken & Root Vegetable Roast
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken leg quarter, its skin crisped to a deep golden-brown, rests centrally on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a warm beige hue. Around it, rustic chunks of roasted carrots, parsnips, and potatoes, boasting caramelized edges and earthy tones, are arranged organically, not stacked, allowing for natural negative space. A vibrant, smooth dollop of bright green fermented greens puree is placed cleanly to the side, offering a striking color contrast. The plating is minimalistic and unforced, highlighting the natural beauty of each ingredient. A few delicate fresh herb leaves are scattered naturally on or beside the chicken. The scene is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, illuminated by soft natural light. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige lies simply beside the plate, with a clean, unobtrusive background featuring subtle out-of-focus green foliage, reinforcing the eco-conscious aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Fermented cabbage or other fermented vegetable, squeezed

instructions: Place chicken in a large container. Add fermented brine, peppercorns, and rosemary/thyme. Ensure chicken is submerged. Refrigerate for 24-48 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Drain chicken from brine; pat very dry. Reserve brine for other uses or discard.
In a large roasting tray, toss carrots, parsnips, and potatoes with olive oil, salt, and pepper.

Place chicken on top of root vegetables in the tray. Roast for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Skin should be golden and crisp. Turn vegetables once during roasting.
While chicken roasts, blanch greens in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until tender. Drain well and squeeze out excess water. Reserve stems for stock.
In a food processor, combine blanched greens, fermented cabbage, minced garlic, olive oil, and vegetable stock. Process until a smooth puree forms. Season with salt.
Remove chicken and vegetables from oven. Let chicken rest for 10 minutes.
Serve chicken with roasted root vegetables and a generous dollop of fermented greens puree. Garnish with fresh herb leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: Tagliatelle is coiled neatly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pasta is evenly coated in a creamy, rich sauce. Seared chicken breast, cut into thick chunks, is nestled among the pasta. Sliced cremini mushrooms are integrated throughout the dish. Fresh chopped parsley and a light grating of Parmesan cheese provide vibrant green and pale yellow accents. The dish displays warm golden, earthy brown, and creamy white tones. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a cotton napkin and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. A single refined restaurant portion is presented.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Slice 300g cremini mushrooms. Mince 3 garlic cloves. Dice 1 medium onion. Cut 500g chicken breast into 3cm thick chunks.

Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the pan. Sauté diced onion for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Pour in 250ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in 200ml heavy cream. Simmer gently for 2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, cook 400g tagliatelle in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120ml pasta water.

Return cooked chicken to the pan with the sauce. Add drained tagliatelle. Add 50g grated Parmesan cheese and 15g chopped fresh parsley. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pot Lemon Herb Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous individual portion of One-Pot Lemon Herb Chicken and Rice is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, skin side up, is positioned centrally, slightly overlapping a mound of fluffy, pale yellow rice. The rice, cooked to absorb the flavorful broth, shows flecks of green chopped parsley and minced garlic. Thin, translucent slices of cooked lemon are nestled among the rice and beside the chicken. The chicken thigh exhibits a crisp, inviting skin texture and is cooked through, revealing tender meat. The overall arrangement is natural and comforting, with ingredients settling organically. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, soft kitchen light. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate on a casually placed cloth napkin. The background is a relaxed family dining area with a lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, dried oregano, and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the long-grain white rice. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add lemon slices.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in fresh lemon juice and chopped parsley. Fluff rice with a fork.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Apple and Honey Velouté
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Savory Apple and Honey Velouté is presented in a clean, matte white ceramic bowl. The soup is a smooth, velvety liquid, exhibiting a warm, pale golden-beige color. Its surface is perfectly unblemished, indicating a finely puréed and strained consistency. Garnishing the center are irregular, rustic chunks of deeply golden-brown crispy prosciutto, providing a textural contrast. Alongside the prosciutto, a few vibrant, dark green, whole crispy sage leaves are artfully placed, offering a pop of color and an aromatic element. The bowl is positioned on a natural light wood table surface, subtly textured. A neatly folded, light gray cotton napkin rests to the left of the bowl. Simple, modern silver flatware is placed to the right. The background is a softly blurred, warm-toned restaurant interior, maintaining a casual bistro ambiance with natural, even lighting that highlights the soup's inviting warmth.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lay prosciutto slices flat on a baking sheet. Bake 10-12 minutes until very crisp. Cool. Crumble into small, irregular chunks. Set aside.
In a large pot, melt 15 g butter with olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced apples. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly softened.
Pour in stock and honey. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 15-20 minutes until apples are very tender.

Remove from heat. Carefully blend soup with an immersion blender until completely smooth. Alternatively, transfer to a stand blender and blend in batches. For a truly smooth velouté, pass soup through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot.
Return soup to low heat. Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Heat through gently; do not boil.
In a small pan, melt remaining 15 g butter over medium-low heat. Add sage leaves. Fry 1-2 minutes per side until crisp. Remove and drain on paper towel.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with crumbled crispy prosciutto and a few fried sage leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Cherry Clafoutis
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Cherry Clafoutis is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic ramekin, resting on a flat, natural cream-colored ceramic plate. The clafoutis itself is golden-brown on top with slightly puffed edges, revealing a creamy, off-white custard interior. Whole, dark red fresh cherries are visibly scattered within the custard. A few vibrant, ruby-red fermented cherries are artfully placed on top of the clafoutis, adding a contrasting texture and tangy visual pop. The composition is clean and minimalistic, with ample negative space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly placed beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting its organic textures. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of soft green foliage from a houseplant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm, as is, or with a very light dusting of powdered sugar for a traditional touch.
Enjoy as a light dessert after a meal.
instructions: Pit 100g of cherries. Reserve all cherry pits.

Place pitted cherries in a clean jar. Combine 100ml water and 2g sea salt to create a brine. Pour brine over cherries. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly bubbly and tangy. Refrigerate.
Rinse remaining cherry pits. Combine pits with oat milk in a small saucepan. Heat gently for 10 minutes. Do not boil. Strain milk, discard pits. This is your cherry pit infused milk.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly butter four 150ml ramekins.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Add eggs one at a time, whisking until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the cherry pit infused milk and vanilla extract until batter is smooth.
Distribute remaining 200g fresh pitted cherries evenly among the buttered ramekins.
Pour batter over cherries in each ramekin.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until clafoutis is set and lightly golden brown around the edges. A knife inserted near the center should come out clean.
Serve warm, topped with a few fermented cherries.
notes: This recipe utilizes a zero-waste approach by infusing the cherry pits into the milk, adding a subtle almond-like flavor. Ensure pits are thoroughly rinsed.
The fermented cherries add a delightful tangy counterpoint to the sweet clafoutis. Adjust fermentation time to your preferred tartness.
For a richer flavor, consider using grass-fed butter for greasing ramekins. For a plant-based alternative, use coconut oil.
Coconut sugar or maple syrup can be used as natural sweetener alternatives to granulated sugar.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Salmon Rice Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Cheesy Chicken and Salmon Rice Bake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The baked rice forms the foundation, its tender grains infused with savory spices, creating a comforting, slightly irregular mound. Nestled within the rice are substantial, irregular chunks of seared chicken, displaying a golden-brown crust, and generous flakes of cooked salmon, their natural pink-orange hues providing a visual contrast. A melted layer of golden-orange shredded cheddar cheese cascades over the rice, creating a bubbly, inviting top, with some areas of deeper browning for texture. Perched casually on top of the rice bake is a single sunny-side-up fried egg, its vibrant yellow yolk glistening and edges slightly crispy, ready to be broken. Beside the egg, a small, natural heap of fresh apple-jalapeno relish adds a vibrant pop of bright green and crisp white, offering a fresh, slightly spicy and sweet counterpoint to the warm, rich tones of the bake. The components are naturally portioned, touching and slightly overlapping, reflecting a homely, unpretentious plating style. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting, enhancing the cozy, lived-in atmosphere. A simple, plain cloth napkin is casually draped beside the plate, with a basic, everyday fork resting on it. The background is minimal, hinting at a comfortable family kitchen setting without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served family-style directly from the baking dish
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice chicken into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken. Sear until browned on all sides. Cook to 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.

Place salmon fillet on a baking sheet. Drizzle with a small amount of olive oil. Bake in preheated oven for 12-15 minutes, or until cooked through and flakes easily. Let cool slightly. Flake salmon into large pieces.
Dice onion into small cubes. Mince garlic. Finely dice one jalapeno, remove seeds for less heat if desired.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and diced jalapeno. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, and chili powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until rice is lightly toasted.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in seared chicken and flaked salmon.
Cover skillet. Transfer to preheated oven. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove skillet from oven. Stir gently. Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the top.
Return to oven, uncovered. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
While rice bakes, prepare apple-jalapeno relish. Finely dice remaining jalapeno. Dice apple into small cubes.
In a small bowl, combine diced apple, diced jalapeno, and fresh lime juice. Stir well.
In a separate pan, fry 4 eggs sunny-side up or to desired doneness.
Serve warm rice bake directly from the skillet or spoon into individual bowls. Top each serving with a fried egg and a spoonful of apple-jalapeno relish.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Adjust jalapeno quantity for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Red Onion Tarte Tatin with Honey-Thyme Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly presented wedge of Caramelized Red Onion Tarte Tatin rests on a pristine round white porcelain dessert plate. The top layer showcases deeply caramelized red onion slices, their natural rings visible, radiating a rich, glossy amber-brown hue from the honey-thyme glaze. The onions are tender, glistening, and slightly collapsed from the cooking process. Beneath, the golden-brown puff pastry crust is visibly flaky and crisp, providing a textural contrast. A light scattering of fresh green thyme leaves adorns the surface, adding a subtle pop of color and aromatic freshness. The plate has ample negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and polished dessert fork are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its refined sweetness and professional presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a dollop of crème fraîche or a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Slice red onions thinly into rings.
Melt butter in a 24cm oven-safe, non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add sliced onions. Cook for 15-20 minutes until very soft and translucent.
Stir in brown sugar and balsamic vinegar. Continue cooking for 10-15 minutes until onions are deeply caramelized and sticky. Set aside to cool slightly.
Lightly grease the same pan if needed.
Arrange the caramelized onions evenly in the bottom of the pan.
Roll out puff pastry. Cut a circle slightly larger than the pan. Place pastry over the onions, tucking edges down around the sides.
Whisk egg yolk with a teaspoon of water. Brush pastry with egg wash.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and puffed.
Remove from oven. Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes.
Place a serving plate over the pan. Carefully invert the tarte tatin onto the plate.
While tart bakes, combine honey and leaves from 2 thyme sprigs in a small saucepan. Gently heat until honey is fluid. Do not boil.
Brush the warm tarte tatin with the honey-thyme glaze.
Garnish with remaining fresh thyme leaves. Serve warm.
notes: This dessert is best served warm to enjoy the full flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Corn and Rice Salad with Cheddar
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of Corn and Rice Salad with Cheddar is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The salad forms a vibrant mound, showcasing a colorful medley of textures. Fluffy white Basmati rice serves as the base, interspersed with bright yellow corn kernels, small cubes of vibrant red and green bell peppers, finely diced red onion, and creamy yellow cubes of sharp cheddar cheese. Each component is clearly visible, with some pieces slightly overlapping, creating a natural, unpretentious look. A light, glossy dressing coats the ingredients, and flecks of fresh green chopped parsley are scattered throughout and on top, adding a fresh accent. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a comfortable family kitchen setting. A basic fork is placed beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors and inviting textures of the homemade salad. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the comforting dish.

ingredients.name: Red Bell Pepper, diced into small cubes
Green Bell Pepper, diced into small cubes
Sharp Cheddar Cheese, diced into small cubes

instructions: Prepare the rice. Cook Basmati rice according to package directions. Let it cool completely.
Prepare vegetables. Finely dice the red onion. Dice red and green bell peppers into small cubes. Mince the garlic.
Drain canned corn well. Dice cheddar cheese into small cubes. Chop fresh parsley.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, Dijon mustard, white wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper.
Combine salad ingredients. In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, drained corn, diced red onion, diced bell peppers, minced garlic, and diced cheddar cheese.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Serve immediately or chill before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage & Lentil Fermented Root Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone, like cream or beige. The composition is minimalistic, honoring each ingredient's natural beauty. A mound of vibrant, mixed greens forms the base, showcasing finely shredded fermented green cabbage and julienned pickled orange carrots. Scattered among these are deep crimson diced beetroot cubes and small, firm brown lentils, adding pops of color and grounding texture. A light sheen of vinaigrette coats the ingredients, reflecting soft natural light. Freshly chopped parsley and dill are sparingly sprinkled over the top, offering a final fresh green touch. The plate is clean, with ample white space. The setting features a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and a subtle background of blurred green foliage, emphasizing sustainability and nature.

ingredients.name: Beetroot
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium, peeled and diced into 1 cm cubes

instructions: Wash and sterilize a 1-liter glass jar.
Shred cabbage thinly. Slice carrots thinly.
Combine shredded cabbage and sliced carrots in the jar. Add garlic and dill sprigs.
Dissolve salt in filtered water to make a brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermenting weight.
Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Let ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 3-7 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate once fermented.
Rinse lentils. Combine lentils and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender but not mushy.
Drain excess water. Set aside to cool.
Dice beetroot into 1 cm cubes.
Steam or lightly boil beetroot cubes for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp.
Drain and cool.
In a small bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, salt, and pepper.
Gradually whisk in olive oil until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine cooled lentils, cooled beetroot cubes, and about 200g of the drained pickled cabbage and carrots.
Add chopped fresh parsley and dill.
Pour vinaigrette over salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
notes: Fermented vegetables can be prepared well in advance, improving flavor over time.
This recipe is highly adaptable; use seasonal vegetables available locally.
Any leftover pickling brine can be used in dressings or as a gut-healthy tonic.
Save vegetable scraps for homemade vegetable broth to reduce waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Tomato Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, clear amber soup presented in a pristine white porcelain bowl. The broth is rich and inviting. Tender shredded chicken pieces, approximately 1-2 cm in length, are evenly distributed throughout. Bright red diced tomato cubes, about 1 cm, add pops of color and texture. Individual grains of fluffy white long-grain rice are visible, suspended in the savory liquid. A generous sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley leaves adorns the surface, providing a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the soup's fresh ingredients and appealing warmth in a casual bistro setting. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a relaxed restaurant atmosphere without distracting from the dish.
instructions: Place chicken breasts in a pot. Cover with 1 litre of chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature, about 15-20 minutes.
Remove chicken. Shred or dice into 1-2 cm pieces. Set aside. Strain broth and reserve.
In a large soup pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in remaining 500ml chicken broth, reserved chicken broth, and canned diced tomatoes with their juice. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in rice. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Return shredded chicken to the pot. Stir in hot sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer 5 minutes to heat through.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or cilantro. Serve with lemon wedges if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Garlic Parmesan Linguine
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white porcelain dinner plate cradles a generous portion of creamy linguine, elegantly coiled into a neat mound at the center. The pasta gleams with a rich, ivory sauce, subtly speckled with finely chopped green parsley and delicate white strands of melted Parmesan. Beside the pasta, two substantial, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast medallions, each halved diagonally, rest prominently. Their perfectly seared crust contrasts with the tender, juicy interior. A sprinkle of vibrant green parsley and a dusting of freshly shaved Parmesan adorn the chicken and pasta. The presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional European flatware, under soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer a bowl of extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a crisp, light Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 100g, freshly grated, plus extra for serving

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest on cutting board.
While chicken rests, cook linguine in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
In the same skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Gradually whisk in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency.
Add drained linguine to the sauce. Toss to coat pasta evenly.
Slice rested chicken breasts diagonally into thick medallions. Do not fan.
Plate pasta onto individual dishes. Arrange chicken medallions beside or on top of pasta.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The reserved pasta water is key for adjusting the sauce's consistency and helping it emulsify.
For best results, use freshly grated Parmesan cheese, not pre-grated.
traditional_techniques: Mantecare: The process of vigorously tossing pasta with sauce and cheese, often with a little pasta water, to create a creamy, emulsified coating.
Al Dente: Cooking pasta until it is firm to the bite, ensuring optimal texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Schnitzel with Dill Potato Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown Pork Schnitzel, pounded thin and pan-fried to a crisp texture, is centrally placed on a clean white round porcelain plate. Its light golden hue has subtle darker brown edges. Beside it, a neatly mounded portion of Dill Potato Salad features soft white potato 2cm cubes, generously flecked with vibrant green chopped dill and finely diced red onion. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests atop the schnitzel. The dish showcases golden-brown, creamy white, fresh green, and bright yellow colors. Textures include the schnitzel's crispy exterior and tender interior, contrasting with the soft, yielding potato salad. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface, with a crisp white cotton napkin nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting textures in a professional, approachable restaurant style.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Lemon wedge
Lingonberry jam (optional)
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain well.
While potatoes are warm, combine with finely diced red onion and finely chopped dill.
Whisk white wine vinegar, olive oil, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper for dressing.
Pour dressing over warm potatoes. Toss gently. Set aside.
Place pork cutlets between two sheets of cling film. Pound evenly to 3-4mm thickness.
Season both sides of pork with salt and pepper.
Set up breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, allowing excess to drip off.
Press firmly into breadcrumbs, ensuring full coverage.
Heat neutral oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat (oil should be about 2-3cm deep).
Fry schnitzel one or two at a time, without overcrowding, for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer fried schnitzel to a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve immediately with a generous portion of dill potato salad and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Seared Chicken with Fermented Chili Salsa and Crispy Rice
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white ceramic plate presents a golden-brown seared chicken thigh, whole and resting on irregularly shaped, crispy brown rice pieces. Beside it, a vibrant, reddish-orange fermented chili salsa is generously spooned, its slightly chunky texture adding depth. Scattered across the plate are bright pops of color and texture: golden charred corn kernels, small cubes of fresh red bell pepper, and delicate, paper-thin slivers of red onion, offering a refreshing crunch. Fresh green coriander leaves provide a final touch. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space, emphasizing the natural beauty of each ingredient. The eco-conscious setting features a light reclaimed wood surface and a natural beige linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, enhancing its organic appeal.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Chili Salsa (Start 5-7 days in advance):
Roughly chop 300g tomatoes, half of red onion, half of red bell pepper, 2 garlic cloves, and 1 chili.
Combine chopped vegetables and 10g sea salt in a clean jar.
Add filtered water to cover vegetables completely.
Place a fermentation weight or small bag of water on top to keep vegetables submerged.
Cover jar loosely with a lid or cloth.
Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days. Burp daily.
Once fermented (slightly tangy, bubbly), blend mixture until smooth or slightly chunky. Taste and adjust seasoning. Store in refrigerator.
Cook Rice:
Rinse 200g brown rice.
Combine rice with 400ml water and a pinch of salt in a pot.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover.
Simmer for 30-35 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Fluff with a fork. Spread cooked rice thinly on a baking sheet to cool and dry slightly.
Prepare Chicken:
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Rest for 5 minutes.
Make Crispy Rice:
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add cooled, dried rice to the pan, pressing down slightly to form a single layer.
Cook for 8-10 minutes, without stirring, until bottom layer is golden and crispy.
Break into large, irregular pieces.
Prepare Fresh Components:
Carefully cut kernels from corn cob. Lightly char corn kernels in a dry pan or under a grill until slightly browned.
Finely dice remaining red bell pepper.
Thinly slice remaining red onion.
Chop fresh coriander or parsley.
Plate the Dish:
Place a portion of crispy rice on each plate.
Arrange one seared chicken thigh on top of the rice.
Spoon generous amounts of fermented chili salsa alongside and partially over the chicken.
Scatter charred corn kernels, diced fresh bell pepper, and thinly sliced red onion over and around the dish.
Garnish with fresh coriander or parsley leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Garlic, Broccoli, and Sun-Dried Tomato
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, centered on a clean white porcelain plate. Alongside, vibrant green broccoli florets are lightly sautéed, retaining their firm texture and bright color. Diced caramelized onions and minced garlic are interspersed among the broccoli, adding depth. Thinly sliced, rehydrated sun-dried tomatoes provide bursts of deep red, contrasting with the green and golden tones. A light, savory pan sauce, infused with garlic and chicken broth, pools subtly around the base. The dish is garnished with freshly chopped green basil leaves, providing a final touch of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware beside it, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in white wine to deglaze the pan. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add broccoli florets and chicken broth to the pan. Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until broccoli is tender-crisp.
Stir in the sliced sun-dried tomatoes.
Return the cooked chicken breasts to the pan. Heat through for 1-2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped basil or parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Baltic Sausage and Potato Beer Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baltic Sausage and Potato Beer Bake is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic gratin dish. Layers of tender, golden-brown potato slices (5mm thick) and robust, browned sausage chunks (2cm thick) are visible, interwoven with beer-caramelized onions. A rich, bubbly, golden-orange cheese sauce, lightly browned on top, covers the dish. The creamy American cheese sauce provides a smooth, golden blanket. The dish features warm golden-brown, deep amber, and rich brown tones. Textures include tender potatoes, juicy sausage, and creamy sauce with a slight top crispness. Freshly chopped parsley adds a vibrant green garnish. The gratin dish rests on a light wooden table. A folded linen napkin and standard flatware are placed alongside. Soft, natural lighting highlights the dish's comforting appeal in a modern bistro setting, with a subtle background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Pickled cucumbers
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 5 mm thick rounds. Place in cold water.
Heat oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook, stirring, until deeply caramelized, about 15-20 minutes.
Remove onions from skillet. Add sausages to the same skillet. Brown on all sides. Remove sausages and slice into 2 cm thick pieces.
Return caramelized onions to the skillet. Add minced garlic and fresh thyme sprigs. Pour in dark beer. Bring to a simmer, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Drain potatoes well. Layer half the potato slices in the bottom of the skillet or a 20x30 cm baking dish. Arrange half the sliced sausages over the potatoes. Pour half the beer-onion mixture over.
In a small saucepan, gently heat heavy cream. Add American cheese slices. Stir until cheese is completely melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Layer remaining potatoes over the sausage. Arrange remaining sausage pieces on top. Pour the remaining beer-onion mixture evenly over. Pour the melted cheese sauce over the entire dish.

Cover the baking dish tightly with foil. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 40 minutes. Remove foil. Continue baking for another 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the top is golden and bubbly.
Let the bake rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: For best results, use a high-quality smoked pork sausage traditional to Baltic regions, such as a kielbasa or a robust farmer's sausage.

recipes.recipe_name: Chuncheon Dakgalbi (Spicy Stir-fried Chicken)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chuncheon Dakgalbi is presented on a simple, round, deep Korean ceramic plate, showcasing its vibrant red-orange color. Bite-sized chicken chunks, coated in the spicy sauce, are nestled amongst large, tender squares of cabbage and thick, soft slices of sweet potato. Onion wedges and lengths of green onion are visible throughout the dish. The ingredients are casually arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a natural, hearty mound. A light sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds and a few fresh, roughly torn perilla leaves garnish the top, adding a touch of green and a nutty aroma. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside metal chopsticks and a small white rice bowl. A couple of small, traditional banchan bowls, perhaps holding kimchi and pickled radish, are placed nearby. Warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Offer various banchan (side dishes) like kimchi and pickled radishes.
Provide fresh lettuce or perilla leaves for ssam (wraps), allowing diners to wrap the chicken and rice.
Traditionally enjoyed communally, often cooked at the table on a portable burner.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm bite-sized chunks.
In a large bowl, combine gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, minced garlic, minced ginger, sesame oil, and black pepper. Mix well to form the marinade.
Add chicken chunks to the marinade. Mix thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.
Peel and slice sweet potato into 0.5 cm thick rounds.
Cut cabbage into large 4-5 cm squares.
Slice onion into thick wedges.
Cut green onions into 5 cm lengths.
If using, separate tteok.
Heat a large skillet or wide pan over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is mostly cooked through and browned.
Add sweet potato, cabbage, onion, and tteok (if using) to the pan. Continue to stir-fry, mixing all ingredients well with the sauce.
Cover the pan and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender and chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Stir in green onions and perilla leaves (if using) during the last minute of cooking.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust gochugaru to control spice level.
For an even richer dish, add a small amount of cheese over the top during the last few minutes of cooking, melting it over the hot dakgalbi.
Leftovers can be mixed with rice and seaweed flakes to make bokkeumbap (fried rice) directly in the pan.
traditional_techniques: Stir-frying (bokkeum) in a large, wide pan

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom Stroganoff with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a generous, yet refined, individual portion of al dente pappardelle pasta, twirled into an elegant mound on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Each broad ribbon of pasta is generously coated in a luscious, creamy, pale-yellow sauce. Sautéed cremini mushroom slices and finely diced caramelized onions are visibly interspersed throughout the pasta and gently arranged on top, showcasing their earthy brown hues. A light sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped dill provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness. The sauce has a smooth, velvety texture, while the mushrooms offer a tender bite. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and a neatly folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled cucumbers or gherkins for a traditional acidic contrast.
Offer crusty rye bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions until al dente.
Reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, slice mushrooms thinly.
Dice onion finely. Mince garlic.
Heat vegetable oil and 15 grams butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove mushrooms from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 grams butter to the skillet. Add diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 4-5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, creating a roux.
Gradually whisk in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in sour cream until smooth. Do not boil.
Return cooked mushrooms to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Add drained pasta to the skillet. Toss to coat evenly with the sauce.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Chop fresh dill. Stir half into the pasta. Reserve remaining for garnish.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh dill.
traditional_techniques: Sautéing vegetables to build flavor base
Creating a roux for sauce thickening

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Cheek with Pickled Kohlrabi
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial portion of slow-cooked beef cheek, deep mahogany brown with a slightly crisp exterior, rests prominently on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The beef is presented as a whole, tender chunk. Beside it, a smooth, artfully swirled mound of creamy white parsnip puree provides a soft contrast. Thin, translucent rounds of pale green pickled kohlrabi are meticulously arranged to add a vibrant, fresh element and visual texture. A delicate sprinkle of finely chopped chives garnishes the beef, adding a subtle touch of green. The plate is set on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in a soft beige. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and natural colors. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the dish to be the sole focus.

ingredients.name: Rendered beef fat or olive oil

instructions: Preheat oven to 140°C. Trim excess fat from beef cheeks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over high heat. Add a splash of beef fat or oil. Sear beef cheeks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef.

Add remaining beef fat or oil to the pot. Place seared beef cheeks back in. Add garlic cloves, thyme sprigs, bay leaves, and black peppercorns. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in fat. Add more fat if needed.
Cover pot tightly. Slow cook in the preheated oven for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Remove from oven. Let beef cool in its fat. Refrigerate overnight for best flavor and texture.
For pickled kohlrabi: Peel kohlrabi. Cut into thin rounds or small batons.
In a small saucepan, combine water, white wine vinegar, sugar, and salt for pickling liquid. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat.
Place kohlrabi in a heat-proof jar or bowl. Pour hot pickling liquid over kohlrabi. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
For parsnip puree: Peel and chop parsnips into 2 cm pieces. Place in a saucepan. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain parsnips. Return to saucepan. Mash or blend until smooth. Add butter or cream, salt, and pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with a little cooking liquid if needed.
To serve: Gently reheat beef cheeks in their fat on the stovetop or in the oven until warmed through. If desired, sear briefly in a hot pan to crisp the exterior.
Plate a single beef cheek. Spoon a generous portion of parsnip puree beside it. Arrange several pickled kohlrabi rounds or batons artfully next to the puree. Garnish with chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef with Caramelized Onions is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A large, rustic chunk of dark brown, fork-tender braised beef, its surface glistening, is positioned slightly off-center. Beneath and around the beef is a generous bed of deeply caramelized, soft, golden-brown onion slices, showing their rich, glossy texture. A dark, glossy, rich pan sauce is artfully spooned over the beef and pooled around the base, creating a sheen. A small sprig of fresh thyme rests gently on top of the beef, adding a touch of green. The overall presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. The scene is illuminated with natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dredge beef in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Add a pinch of sugar if needed to aid caramelization.
Add chopped carrots, celery, and minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes until vegetables soften slightly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, reducing slightly.
Pour in beef broth. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef chunks to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in liquid. Cover the pot with a lid.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Carefully remove beef from the pot. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.

Skim any excess fat from the strained liquid. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until the sauce slightly thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Stir in butter. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve each beef chunk with a generous portion of the caramelized onions and a ladle of the rich pan sauce.
notes: For best flavor, braise the beef a day in advance. Cool completely, then refrigerate. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the oven.
Adjust the consistency of the sauce by reducing it further for a thicker glaze or adding a splash of broth for a thinner consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ragù con Orecchiette
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Pollo al Ragù con Orecchiette is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed. Tender, shredded chicken pieces are generously mixed throughout the al dente orecchiette pasta, coated in a rich, deep red tomato ragù. The sauce is rustic, with visible finely diced carrot, celery, and onion, creating a harmonious texture. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano covers the top, adding a creamy white contrast. Fresh green oregano leaves are scattered lightly for color and aroma. The dish maintains a natural, inviting form, avoiding rigid shapes, with moderate negative space around the edges. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its vibrant colors and inviting textures. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for soaking up the ragù.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Accompany with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.

ingredients.name: Fresh oregano or basil leaves, for garnish

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and aromatic. This is the soffritto base.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Return seared chicken to the pot.
Add chicken stock. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 45-60 minutes. Cook until chicken is very tender and easily shredded.
Remove chicken from the sauce. Using two forks, shred the chicken into smaller pieces. Return shredded chicken to the sauce. Stir well.
While ragù simmers, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add orecchiette pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving about 60 ml of pasta water. Add drained pasta directly to the chicken ragù. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Stir in 60 g of grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese. Toss thoroughly to coat pasta and chicken.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining Parmigiano-Reggiano and fresh oregano or basil leaves.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality canned tomatoes.
Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The ragù can be made ahead of time and reheated; flavors often improve the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Carne Asada with Pico de Gallo and Cilantro Lime Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared beef chunks, cooked to a perfect medium-rare, is centrally arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef exhibits a dark, caramelized crust and a tender, pink interior. Adjacent to the beef, a vibrant scoop of fresh pico de gallo showcases finely diced red tomatoes, white onion, and green jalapeños, studded with bright green cilantro. A crisp mound of mixed salad greens, lightly dressed with a cilantro-lime vinaigrette, completes the arrangement. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and a small ceramic bowl of warm corn tortillas beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s fresh colors and varied textures, creating an inviting, authentic Mexican casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Offer extra lime wedges
instructions: Slice beef against the grain into 2cm thick pieces.
Combine juice from 2 limes, 30ml olive oil, minced garlic, cumin, chili powder, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Add beef to marinade. Toss to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, up to 4 hours, refrigerated.
Finely dice tomatoes, red onion, and jalapeños for Pico de Gallo.
Chop half of the cilantro. Combine diced vegetables and cilantro with juice from 1 lime and salt. Mix well.
Wash and dry salad greens.
For vinaigrette, whisk juice from remaining 1 lime, 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Heat a cast iron skillet or grill over high heat until very hot.
Sear marinated beef pieces for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness.
Remove beef from heat. Rest for 5 minutes.
Slice rested beef into serving portions.
Toss salad greens with cilantro lime vinaigrette.
Plate beef chunks with a generous scoop of Pico de Gallo and a side of dressed salad greens.
notes: For best flavor, marinate beef for at least 2 hours.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon-Herb Pasta with Seared Apples and White Wine
recipes.visual_description: The Lemon-Herb Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally positioned. Al dente linguine is lightly twirled, forming a modest mound, glistening with a delicate, bright lemon-white wine sauce. Interspersed throughout the pasta are golden-brown seared apple wedges, their edges subtly caramelized, adding warmth and texture. Freshly chopped mint leaves are scattered over the dish, providing vibrant green pops against the pale pasta and golden apples. A few whole mint leaves and fine lemon zest are artfully placed as garnish. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh, appealing colors and inviting textures against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve 150ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, prepare apples. Core apples. Cut into 1 cm thick wedges.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add apple wedges. Sprinkle lightly with sugar.
Sear apples 3-4 minutes per side until golden and slightly tender. Remove from skillet.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Add minced garlic and diced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour in white wine. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add drained pasta to skillet. Add lemon juice and zest. Add reserved pasta water. Toss well to combine.
Return seared apples to skillet. Gently toss with pasta.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Finely chop fresh mint leaves. Stir half into pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh mint leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork and Mushroom Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Spicy Pork and Mushroom Pasta Bake rests on a simple, rustic ceramic plate on a well-used wooden dining table. The cooked penne pasta is coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce, studded with tender 2cm cubes of browned pork and thick slices of sautéed mushrooms. A generous layer of melted, golden-brown cheddar cheese bubbles on top, showing slight charring at the edges. The dish is casually garnished with a scattering of crisp, golden-brown crushed corn tortilla pieces and a zigzag drizzle of creamy, pale orange spicy mayonnaise. A few fresh green coriander leaves are sprinkled over. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen light, highlighting the comforting textures and vibrant colors of the dish, ready for a family meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown pork cubes on all sides. Remove pork from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thickly sliced mushrooms. Sauté until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 7 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chili powder, cumin, oregano, 30ml hot sauce, salt, and pepper. Bring sauce to a simmer.
Return browned pork to the sauce. Simmer for 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir cooked pasta into the sauce with pork and vegetables. Mix thoroughly.
Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the top of the pasta mixture. Do not stir.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, until cheese is melted and bubbly with golden edges.
While pasta bakes, cut corn tortillas into small triangles. Fry or bake until crisp and golden. Drain excess oil.
Mix mayonnaise with additional hot sauce to taste for a spicy mayo drizzle.
Serve hot, topped with crisp tortilla pieces, spicy mayo drizzle, and fresh chopped coriander.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Potato Salad with Lemon Herb Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on an everyday ceramic plate, sitting on a well-used wooden dining table. Roasted baby potato halves, golden-brown and tender, are scattered among vibrant green, slightly charred broccoli florets. Small, irregularly diced chicken pieces are nestled throughout, showing a light golden sear. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes and thin slices of red onion add pops of color. The salad is casually arranged, with components naturally overlapping, and glistening lightly with a lemon-herb vinaigrette. A simple fork and a crumpled cloth napkin rest beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the homely scene, emphasizing the comforting textures and natural colors of the ingredients. The plate is adequately filled, leaving some negative space around the edges.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Halve baby potatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast for 20 minutes.

Toss broccoli florets with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add to the baking sheet with potatoes. Continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, until potatoes are tender and broccoli is slightly charred.
While vegetables roast, dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt, pepper, and 5 ml olive oil.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook for 6-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Set aside to cool slightly.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 25 ml olive oil, juice from the lemon, Dijon mustard, and dried oregano in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine roasted potatoes, roasted broccoli, cooked chicken, halved cherry tomatoes, and sliced red onion.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Chop fresh parsley. Sprinkle over the salad before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Stacked Tomato, Rice & Cheese Tortilla Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of a golden-baked Stacked Tomato, Rice & Cheese Tortilla Bake sits slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The bake is composed of several distinct layers: soft corn tortillas, fluffy rice infused with vibrant diced tomatoes and aromatic spices, and generous amounts of melted, bubbly Monterey Jack cheese, with the top layer beautifully golden and slightly crisped. A subtle pool of rich, savory tomato liquid from the bake gathers around its base. The dish is generously garnished with bright green, freshly chopped cilantro. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple, light wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and a small ramekin of vibrant red salsa roja. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of authentic salsa roja or salsa verde.
Offer a dollop of crema (Mexican sour cream) or plain Greek yogurt.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
Serve with a side of refried beans or black beans.

ingredients.name: Small corn or flour tortillas (approx. 15 cm diameter)
Shredded Monterey Jack or Mexican blend cheese

instructions: Preheat oven to 180 C.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté minced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add diced tomatoes (undrained) and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 15-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Season with salt and pepper.
Lightly grease a baking dish (approx. 20x20 cm).
Place one tortilla in the dish. Spread a layer of rice mixture over it. Sprinkle with a portion of shredded cheese.
Repeat layering: tortilla, rice, cheese. End with a tortilla on top, generously covered with remaining cheese.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and edges are golden.
Let rest 5 minutes. Cut into 4 equal portions.
Serve each portion on a plate. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Chili-Braised Chicken Thighs with Sweet Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chili-Braised Chicken Thighs is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two rich, dark brown chicken thighs, braised to a tender, fall-off-the-bone texture, are positioned slightly overlapping. They retain their whole, rustic shape. Abundant, glossy, deeply caramelized thin onion slices are nestled around and partially beneath the chicken. A generous pour of the dark, glossy braising liquid, infused with chili and beef stock, pools around the chicken and onions. The sauce is thick, coating the ingredients. A scattering of vibrant, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a pop of green. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and inviting presentation.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deeply golden and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add thinly sliced onions to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and tender, about 15-20 minutes.

While onions cook, toast dried Ancho chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Remove from heat. Remove stems and seeds. Place chilies in a bowl and cover with hot water. Let rehydrate for 15 minutes.
Drain rehydrated chilies. Blend chilies with peeled garlic cloves and tomato paste until a smooth paste forms. Add a tablespoon of beef stock if needed to aid blending.
Add chili-garlic paste to the pot with caramelized onions. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in beef stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in liquid. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.

Remove chicken from the pot. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Skim any excess fat from the sauce. If sauce is too thin, simmer on stovetop over medium-high heat until desired consistency. Adjust seasoning.
Serve chicken with the caramelized onions and generous amounts of the braising sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For a spicier dish, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a small amount of a hotter chili like a chipotle chili to the blending paste.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Roasted Beef with Fermented Red Cabbage & Root Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Roasted Beef with Fermented Red Cabbage and Root Puree is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate with ample white space. A large, rustic chunk of deeply browned, slow-roasted beef is positioned centrally. Beside it, a distinct, smooth mound of creamy, pale beige root vegetable puree provides a comforting base. Balancing the composition, a vibrant, ruby-red pile of thinly shredded quick fermented red cabbage adds a striking contrast in color and texture. A glossy, dark brown beef reduction is elegantly drizzled over the beef and sparingly around the plate. The overall plating is minimalistic and clean, highlighting the natural beauty and texture of each ingredient. A single, fresh green thyme sprig rests gently on the beef, offering a subtle pop of color. The dish is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed, natural beige linen napkin is folded neatly to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the rich, earthy tones of the food and natural textures of the setting. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle hint of green from a distant plant, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C.
Pat beef chuck dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chuck on all sides until deeply browned and a crust forms. Remove beef and set aside.
Add sliced onion and whole garlic cloves to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef stock and fresh thyme sprigs.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Slow roast for 3.5 to 4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from the pot. Strain the cooking liquid into a saucepan. Discard solids. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until it thickens into a rich sauce. Season to taste.
For the fermented red cabbage: Thinly shred red cabbage. Place in a bowl. Add 5g of sea salt. Massage cabbage vigorously with hands for 5 minutes until it softens and releases liquid.
Stir in apple cider vinegar. Let sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours, for a quick ferment. Taste and adjust seasoning.
For the root puree: Peel and chop carrots, parsnips, and celeriac into 2 cm chunks.
Place chopped vegetables in a pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain vegetables thoroughly. Return to the pot. Add a splash of the reduced beef stock or a tablespoon of olive oil. Mash or blend until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate: Place a generous mound of root puree off-center on each plate. Cut the beef chuck into large, natural chunks. Place one chunk beside the puree. Add a vibrant pile of the quick fermented red cabbage. Drizzle the rich beef reduction over the beef and around the plate. Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Broccoli and Lemon-Garlic Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken boasts a crisp, savory crust and juicy interior. Beside it, a generous portion of vibrant green roasted broccoli florets are arranged naturally, showing slightly charred edges for texture. A shimmering, pale yellow lemon-garlic butter sauce is spooned artfully over the chicken and around the plate's base, reflecting light. Fresh green parsley is sprinkled over the sauce as a garnish. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a white cotton napkin folded neatly to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting colors and textures, creating a refined yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss broccoli florets with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast broccoli for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Let rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.
Return pan to medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits.
Stir in lemon juice and zest. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk in butter until sauce is slightly thickened. Remove from heat.
Stir in chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Spiced Chicken with Orange and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Moroccan Spiced Chicken with Orange and Tomato is presented in a deep, rustic terracotta-colored ceramic bowl. Two generous, bone-in chicken thighs, seared to golden-brown and braised until fork-tender, are nestled in a rich, reddish-orange sauce. The sauce contains visible soft diced tomatoes and translucent softened onion. Vibrant, tender orange slices are interspersed throughout, adding bright color contrast. Fresh, chopped cilantro and parsley are generously sprinkled over the top, adding verdant freshness. The chicken is moist, and the sauce shimmers. Beside the bowl, a small, fluffy mound of steamed couscous is perfectly portioned. The setting is a warm, simple wooden table, with natural, soft lighting. A subtly patterned linen napkin is neatly folded beside the bowl, completing the authentic, refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with couscous or warm flatbread (khobz).
Offer a side of harissa for those who prefer more heat.
Serve in a communal tagine pot for a traditional family meal.
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, cumin, coriander, ginger, turmeric, and paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown. About 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, orange juice (from 1 orange), chicken stock, and half of the fresh cilantro and parsley. Add saffron if using.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (75°C internal temperature).
Slice remaining orange into rounds. Add orange slices to the pot during the last 15 minutes of cooking.
Adjust seasoning as needed.
Garnish with remaining fresh cilantro and parsley before serving.
notes: Adjust spice levels to personal preference.
Chicken can be marinated overnight for deeper flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Chipotle Chicken with Roasted Corn, Black Bean Salsa & Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A seared, golden-brown chicken breast, cooked whole, anchors the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its surface reveals a slight char and the deep reddish-orange hue of the chipotle marinade. Adjacent to the chicken are irregular, crispy roasted potato wedges, their golden-brown exteriors contrasting with their fluffy interiors. A vibrant mound of black bean and corn salsa sits nearby, showcasing a medley of dark black beans, bright yellow corn kernels, finely diced red onion, and verdant chopped cilantro. The arrangement is organic yet balanced, with moderate negative space. A fresh lime wedge and a few cilantro sprigs garnish the dish. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and even, natural lighting, creating an inviting, authentic Mexican casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Fresh lime wedges
A side of crema or sour cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm wedges or chunks. In a large bowl, toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil, 2.5ml salt, 2.5ml pepper, and 2.5ml cumin. Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and crispy. Stir halfway through.

While potatoes roast, prepare chicken marinade. In a shallow dish, combine minced chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, half of the lime juice, 2.5ml cumin, smoked paprika, 2.5ml salt, 2.5ml pepper, and 15ml olive oil. Add chicken breasts to marinade. Turn to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 15 minutes, or up to 30 minutes in the refrigerator.

For the salsa, combine rinsed black beans, frozen corn kernels, diced red onion, minced garlic, and chopped cilantro in a medium bowl. Add remaining lime juice and 15ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir well. If using fresh corn, roast kernels with potatoes for the last 10 minutes.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes.

To plate, place one whole seared chicken breast on each plate. Arrange a portion of crispy potato wedges beside the chicken. Spoon a generous amount of black bean and corn salsa next to the potatoes. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Forno con Patate e Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Forno con Patate e Pomodoro is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, embodying a simple restaurant-style aesthetic. At the center, one golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, cooked whole, anchors the dish. Surrounding the chicken are tender, roasted potato wedges with slightly crisped edges and bursting, caramelized cherry tomato halves. Thinly sliced, softened onion pieces are interspersed among the vegetables. A light, savory pan sauce, rich with chicken drippings and tomato juices, pools subtly around the base. The dish is generously sprinkled with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, melted and slightly browned in places, and a vibrant scattering of chopped fresh parsley. The colors are earthy and warm: deep golden chicken, rustic brown potatoes, vibrant red tomatoes, and green parsley, all balanced against the white plate. The textures are varied, from crispy chicken skin to soft potato interior and juicy tomatoes. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple mixed green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: New potatoes or small red potatoes
Fresh rosemary, leaves picked and chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and halve potatoes. Quarter cherry tomatoes.
In a large roasting pan, combine halved potatoes, quartered tomatoes, sliced onion, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, thyme, 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat. Spread in a single layer.
Pat chicken thighs thoroughly dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side.
Nestle seared chicken thighs among the vegetables in the roasting pan.
Pour chicken broth into the pan.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender. Chicken skin should be crispy.
Remove pan from oven. Sprinkle grated Parmigiano-Reggiano evenly over chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven for 5 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
