notes: Ensure chicken skin is thoroughly dried before searing for maximum crispness.
Adjust baking time based on the size and thickness of chicken thighs.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Garlic Chicken with Rosemary
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, whole and plump, rests slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A glossy, light amber pan sauce, infused with garlic and rosemary, is generously drizzled over the chicken and pools elegantly around its base. Beside the chicken, a neat cluster of roasted baby potatoes, halved and showing golden, crispy edges, provides an earthy counterpoint. Vibrant green asparagus spears, blanched to tender-crisp perfection, are arranged alongside the potatoes. A small sprig of fresh rosemary garnishes the chicken. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve or quarter baby potatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside and keep warm.
While chicken rests, bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch asparagus spears for 2-3 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Reduce skillet heat to medium. Add minced garlic, rosemary, and thyme to the skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in butter and lemon juice until butter is melted and sauce is emulsified. Taste and adjust seasoning.

To serve, place a pan-seared chicken breast on each plate. Spoon pan sauce generously over chicken. Arrange roasted baby potatoes and blanched asparagus alongside. Garnish with a fresh rosemary sprig if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Beer Braised Chicken with Fermented Root & Aubergine Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh, rich brown and glistening, rests on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. Beside it, a generous, slightly organic mound of fluffy long-grain rice is subtly infused with vibrant, small diced fermented carrots and eggplant, their colors peeking through. The chicken, unsliced, showcases its tender, whole form. Braised eggplant chunks, soft and deep-hued, and thick-cut carrot rounds are nestled around the chicken, lightly coated in the dark beer braising liquid. The plate features ample negative space, highlighting the natural textures and earthy tones of the ingredients. A fresh, delicate sprig of thyme provides a touch of green. The scene is set on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a natural beige linen napkin, under soft, diffused natural light, emphasizing the dish's sustainable simplicity.

ingredients.name: For Fermented Vegetables: Eggplant, diced (1cm cubes)
For Fermented Vegetables: Carrots, diced (1cm cubes)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Vegetables: Dice small eggplant and one carrot into 1cm cubes. Combine water and salt to make a brine. Stir until salt dissolves. Place diced vegetables in a clean glass jar. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small clean rock to keep vegetables under brine. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 5-10 days, or until desired tanginess is reached. Store in refrigerator once fermented.

Sear Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, until deeply golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Sauté Aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Deglaze and Braise: Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken to the pot. Add remaining whole eggplant, cut into large chunks (2-3cm), and remaining carrot, cut into thick rounds (1cm). Add vegetable broth and fresh thyme sprigs. Liquid should partially cover chicken. If not, add more broth or water.
Cook Chicken: Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

Cook Rice: While chicken braises, rinse rice thoroughly. In a separate pot, combine rinsed rice with 600ml water (or a mix of water and some braising liquid for extra flavor). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Combine Rice and Fermented Vegetables: Fluff cooked rice with a fork. Gently fold in 100g of the prepared fermented eggplant and carrot cubes. Adjust seasoning if needed.

Serve: Remove chicken from braising liquid. Spoon a portion of the fermented vegetable rice onto each plate. Place one braised chicken thigh alongside. Spoon some of the braised eggplant and carrot chunks and a little braising liquid over the chicken and rice. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh thyme or finely chopped chives.
notes: For optimal flavor and zero-waste, use homemade vegetable broth made from kitchen scraps (e.g., onion skins, carrot peels, herb stems).
Save chicken bones after braising to make homemade chicken stock for future recipes.
Fermented vegetables can be made weeks in advance and stored in the refrigerator.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Savory Tomato-Onion Ragù and Potato Gratin Crust
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Baked Rigatoni is presented in a shallow, rustic white porcelain bowl. The top features a golden-brown, crispy crust of thinly sliced potatoes, artfully arranged in an overlapping pattern, and toasted Panko breadcrumbs mixed with grated Parmesan. Beneath the crisp topping, the rich, deep reddish-brown tomato-onion ragù, infused with subtle notes of apple, bubbles gently around the edges. Scattered fresh green basil leaves provide a vibrant color contrast and aromatic garnish. The dish is centered on a simple light wooden table, flanked by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the textures and warm colors of the dish, creating an inviting, professional bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread on the side for dipping into any remaining sauce.
instructions: Slice onions thinly. Heat olive oil and butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and very sweet.
Mince garlic. Grate or finely dice the apple. Add minced garlic and prepared apple to the caramelized onions. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring.

Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Season with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Cook for 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce slightly thickens.
While the ragù simmers, preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Cook rigatoni according to package directions, reducing cooking time by 1-2 minutes to ensure it is al dente. Drain pasta.
Lightly grease a 20x30 cm baking dish. Combine the cooked rigatoni with the tomato-onion ragù. Stir in the shredded mozzarella until just combined.
Thinly slice potatoes, preferably using a mandoline. Arrange the potato slices in an overlapping pattern over the pasta mixture in the baking dish.
In a small bowl, mix Panko breadcrumbs with grated Parmesan cheese and a drizzle of olive oil. Sprinkle this mixture evenly over the potato topping.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the potato and breadcrumb topping is golden brown and crispy, and the pasta is bubbling around the edges.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Garnish generously with fresh basil leaves before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Rigatoni with Spicy Italian Sausage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tomato Rigatoni with Spicy Italian Sausage is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rich, vibrant red-orange tomato cream sauce generously coats the ridged rigatoni pasta, which is cooked al dente. Irregularly shaped, browned chunks of spicy Italian sausage are distributed throughout the pasta, providing a hearty texture contrast. A swirl of lighter cream is visible within the sauce, highlighting its richness. Fresh, bright green basil leaves, roughly chopped, are scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. Finely grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the dish. The presentation is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space around the pasta. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. A subtle, out-of-focus background suggests a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Break into small chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage chunks. Cook until browned and cooked through. Break up any large pieces. Remove sausage from skillet. Set aside.
Dice the yellow onion. Mince the garlic cloves.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta water.
Stir heavy cream into the tomato sauce. Return cooked sausage to the skillet. Stir to combine. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Drain pasta. Add cooked rigatoni to the sauce. Toss to coat. Add reserved pasta water as needed for desired consistency.
Grate Parmesan cheese. Roughly chop fresh basil.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil and grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Tomatoes and Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of braised chicken with tomatoes and onions is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate. Two golden-brown chicken thighs, bone-in, are nestled into a rich, rust-red tomato and onion sauce. The sauce features softened diced onion and tender crushed tomato. A few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are casually scattered over the dish. The chicken skin is slightly crisp on top, contrasting with the tender meat. The plate sits on a well-worn light wooden dining table. A simple, folded linen napkin rests beside it. Warm, natural light bathes the scene, creating a cozy, inviting family kitchen atmosphere. The dish exudes homely comfort, with natural ingredient colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown. About 5-7 minutes.
Flip chicken. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Nestle them into the sauce.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Uncover. Increase heat to medium. Simmer for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and sauce thickens slightly.
Check seasoning. Adjust salt and pepper if needed.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve hot.
notes: This dish is even better made ahead and reheated, allowing flavors to deepen.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Lentil and Green Pea Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A clean white porcelain dinner plate holds a generous, fluffy mound of golden-hued pilaf. The basmati rice grains are distinct, intertwined with tender, earthy red lentils and bright green peas. A scattering of deep golden-brown, crispy fried onion slivers crowns the pilaf, adding textural contrast. Fresh, finely chopped green coriander leaves are sprinkled generously over the top, providing a vibrant color pop. The presentation is professional, organized yet organic, with moderate negative space on the plate. Beside the plate, a small, simple white bowl holds a dollop of creamy white raita. The setting is a rustic wooden table with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside cooling Raita (yogurt dip).
Offer Indian pickle (achar) as a condiment.
Accompanied by crisp Papadum.
instructions: Wash basmati rice. Soak in water for 20 minutes. Drain well.
Wash red lentils. Soak in water for 20 minutes. Drain well.
Slice half of the onion thinly into rings.
Heat 15 ml ghee/oil in a small pan. Fry sliced onion until golden brown and crispy. Remove with slotted spoon. Drain on paper towel. Set aside for garnish.
Dice remaining half onion and the tomato.
Heat remaining 15 ml ghee/oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, and cloves. Sauté for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced onion. Sauté for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and slit green chillies. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add diced tomato. Cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and salt. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add drained lentils. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add drained rice and green peas. Gently mix for 1 minute.
Pour in 600 ml hot water. Bring to a boil.

Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-20 minutes until water is absorbed and rice/lentils are tender. (If using pressure cooker, cook for 1 whistle on high, then 5 minutes on low. Let pressure release naturally).
Remove from heat. Let pilaf rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Gently fluff pilaf with a fork. Sprinkle garam masala and half of chopped fresh coriander. Gently mix.
Serve hot. Garnish with remaining fresh coriander and crispy fried onions.
traditional_techniques: Tempering (Tadka): For blooming spices in hot fat.
Dum Cooking: Slow cooking method allowing flavors to meld and rice to steam perfectly.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Beef and Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Rustic Beef and Rice Soup is presented in a deep, slightly chipped ceramic bowl. The rich, reddish-brown broth is brimming with hearty chunks of slow-cooked beef, distinct white grains of tender rice, bright red diced tomatoes, and earthy brown sliced mushrooms. The beef chunks are irregularly cut, showcasing a rustic, home-cooked feel. A sprinkle of vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh parsley floats on top, providing a fresh contrast to the deep colors of the soup. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, sturdy metal spoon rests beside the bowl on a casually folded beige linen napkin. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen, casting soft shadows that enhance the soup's comforting appeal. The scene evokes a relaxed family meal, emphasizing unpretentious, nourishing fare.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, sliced mushrooms, and beef broth.
Bring soup to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1 hour, or until beef is tender. Add water if soup becomes too thick.
Stir in uncooked rice. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.
notes: Beef tenderness is key. Simmer longer if needed for very tender beef.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork Ragu with Pasta and Crispy Tortillas
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty Spicy Pork Ragu with Pasta is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The rich, reddish-brown ragu, featuring tender, shredded pork chunks, diced onion, and sliced mushrooms, coats al dente penne pasta. Vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the top, providing a fresh contrast. A delicate drizzle of creamy, pale orange spicy mayonnaise zigzags across the dish. A generous scattering of golden-brown, crispy tortilla strips adds visual texture and height. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere, ensuring the food remains the focal point.
instructions: Pat pork cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add diced onion and sliced mushrooms. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return pork to the pot. Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, hot sauce, oregano, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily shreddable. Stir occasionally.

While ragu simmers, prepare crispy tortillas. Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss tortilla strips with a drizzle of olive oil. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake for 10-15 minutes, until golden and crispy. Alternatively, shallow fry until crispy.
For spicy mayonnaise: In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, a dash of hot sauce, and lime juice. Season with a pinch of salt.
When ragu is ready, remove bay leaf. Shred pork directly in the pot using two forks. Stir to combine with sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
Add drained pasta to the ragu. Stir well. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen sauce.
Serve ragu and pasta in individual bowls. Top with grated Parmesan cheese, a drizzle of spicy mayonnaise, and a generous sprinkle of crispy tortilla strips and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Pork shoulder can be replaced with pork butt or Boston butt.
Adjust hot sauce to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Rigatoni with Slow-Roasted Tomato, Caramelized Onion, and Crispy Potato Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of rustic rigatoni pasta is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl, set on a simple wooden table surface. The pasta is generously coated in a rich, slightly chunky, deep red slow-roasted tomato and caramelized onion sauce. The rigatoni tubes are plump and al dente, nestled together. Scattered over the pasta are golden-brown, crispy 1 cm potato cubes, offering a delightful textural contrast. Interspersed are golden, apple-infused breadcrumbs, adding another layer of crunch and subtle aroma. A scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped basil and parsley provides a fresh, aromatic garnish. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the dish as the focal point. Natural, even lighting highlights the varied textures and colors. A simple cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl, with a fork, enhancing the modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Halve tomatoes. Slice red onions thinly. Mince garlic.
Spread tomatoes, half the sliced onions, and garlic on a baking tray. Drizzle with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 30-40 minutes until softened and slightly charred.

While tomatoes roast, peel and dice potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add potato cubes. Cook until golden brown and crispy, about 10-12 minutes. Season with salt. Set aside.

Grate stale bread into coarse crumbs. Finely dice the apple. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in the same skillet over medium heat. Add remaining sliced onions and diced apple. Sauté until onions are caramelized and apple is soft, about 15-20 minutes.
Add breadcrumbs to the skillet with caramelized onions and apple. Toast until golden and fragrant, about 5-7 minutes. Set aside. This is your crispy crumble.
Transfer roasted tomatoes, onions, and garlic to a large pot. Crush tomatoes with a spoon. Add red wine vinegar. Simmer gently for 10 minutes. Adjust seasoning. This is your sauce.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta water.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Add reserved pasta water as needed to create a glossy sauce. Toss to coat.
Finely chop fresh basil and parsley. Stir most of the fresh herbs into the pasta. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve hot pasta in individual bowls. Top each portion with crispy potato cubes and the apple-infused breadcrumb crumble. Garnish with remaining fresh herbs. Serve with optional Parmesan cheese.
notes: The apple provides a subtle sweetness and depth to the caramelized onions, not a dominant fruit flavor.
Ensure potatoes are truly crispy for best texture contrast.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto (for sauce base, though modified with roasting)

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Sausage and Potato Roast
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Rustic Sausage and Potato Roast is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate with slight imperfections. Golden-brown roasted potato 2 cm chunks are scattered naturally alongside browned, plump 3 cm sausage pieces. Interspersed are caramelized onion 2 cm wedges and vibrant red bell pepper 2 cm strips, all showing slight charring from roasting. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley adds a pop of color. The dish is arranged casually, with components touching and slightly overlapping, reflecting a homely, comforting meal. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Lighting is soft and inviting, simulating natural kitchen light. A simple, folded cloth napkin rests beside the plate. The background is blurred, focusing solely on the hearty, rustic meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Cut sausages into 3 cm pieces. Cut onion into 2 cm wedges. Cut bell pepper into 2 cm strips.
Place potatoes, sausages, onion, and bell pepper in a large roasting pan.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, dried rosemary, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Toss ingredients thoroughly to coat.
Spread in a single layer in the pan.
Roast 30 minutes. Stir.
Continue roasting 20-30 minutes. Potatoes should be tender. Sausages should be browned. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Serve hot.
notes: This dish is easily adaptable with different types of sausages or vegetables.

recipes.recipe_name: Koji-Marinated Pork Loin with Umami Mushrooms and Black Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone, resting on a light, textured bamboo surface. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene. A generous, irregular mound of light brown black garlic rice forms the base. Beside it, several thick, succulent chunks of golden-brown roasted pork loin are arranged naturally, showcasing their seared crust and tender interior. Scattered around the rice and pork are an assortment of roasted mushrooms—some whole, some halved, some quartered—displaying varied earthy tones of brown and grey, with slightly crinkled, meaty textures. A light sprinkle of thinly sliced green scallions provides a fresh, natural accent. The plating is minimalistic, with ample negative space. A set of simple, elegant wooden chopsticks rests beside the plate on an undyed linen napkin, emphasizing the clean, sustainable aesthetic. The background is clean and uncluttered, with subtle natural elements visible.

ingredients.name: Mixed Mushrooms (shiitake, cremini, oyster)
ingredients.quantity: 400 g, cleaned, larger ones halved or quartered

ingredients.name: Rice Koji (shio koji paste or granular koji)

instructions: Pat pork loin dry. In a shallow dish, combine rice koji, soy sauce, mirin, and grated ginger. Coat pork loin thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for 8-24 hours.

Rinse brown rice. Cook according to package directions. While rice cooks, mash black garlic cloves into a paste. Once rice is cooked and rested, gently fold in black garlic paste and toasted sesame oil. Keep warm.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss mushrooms with 15 ml olive oil, sliced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.

Remove pork from marinade. Scrape off excess koji but do not rinse. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 15-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Use a meat thermometer.
Remove pork from oven. Let rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes. Slice pork into thick, even chunks.

Spoon a mound of black garlic rice onto each handcrafted ceramic plate. Arrange thick pork chunks beside the rice. Scatter roasted mushrooms around the pork and rice. Garnish with thinly sliced scallion greens. Serve immediately.
notes: Utilize mushroom stems by finely chopping and adding to the rice during cooking for extra umami and zero-waste.
Any pork trimmings can be saved for making stock.
Consider sourcing ingredients from local farms to further enhance the eco-conscious aspect.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken Cutlets with Caramelized Onion Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown crispy chicken cutlet, pan-fried to perfection, is elegantly presented on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, pounded thin, has a visibly crunchy breadcrumb crust. Alongside, a generous pool of rich, dark amber caramelized onion jus is spooned, its glossy surface reflecting light. The onions within the jus are visibly soft and deeply browned. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the chicken and jus, adding a pop of green. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits neatly beside the cutlet, ready for a squeeze. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed alongside. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a minimal, blurred background suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Place each breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound chicken to an even 1.5 cm thickness using a meat mallet. Season both sides with salt and black pepper.
Set up a breading station. Place flour in a shallow dish. Place beaten eggs in a second shallow dish. Place Panko breadcrumbs in a third shallow dish.
Dredge each pounded chicken breast in flour. Shake off excess. Dip in beaten egg, ensuring full coverage. Transfer to breadcrumbs. Press firmly to coat evenly. Set aside.

Heat 20g butter and 10ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add thinly sliced onions and thyme sprigs. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Stir occasionally.

Deglaze the pan with white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook for 5-7 minutes until the liquid slightly thickens to a jus consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Remove thyme sprigs.
Heat remaining 30g butter and 20ml olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add breaded chicken cutlets. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Pan-fry chicken for 4-6 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Transfer cooked cutlets to a wire rack to drain excess oil.
Serve crispy chicken cutlets immediately. Spoon generous amounts of caramelized onion jus alongside each cutlet. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Rice Bake with Cheesy Corn Topping
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the Chicken and Rice Bake is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, reflecting a simple restaurant style. The dish features golden-brown, seared chicken thighs, placed atop a bed of creamy, tomato-infused long-grain rice. The rice is studded with vibrant yellow corn kernels and finely diced red tomatoes. A thick, bubbly, golden-brown crust of melted cheese and mayonnaise covers the chicken and parts of the rice, providing a rich texture contrast. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped chives adds a pop of color. The setting is a modern bistro, with the bowl resting on a warm wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and simple silver flatware are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting appeal. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, showcasing the inviting textures and balanced colors.

ingredients.name: Shredded cheddar or mozzarella blend cheese

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice, diced tomatoes (undrained), corn, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice mixture.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise and shredded cheese.
Spread the mayonnaise-cheese mixture evenly over the chicken and rice.
Bake 25-30 minutes, or until rice is tender, liquid is absorbed, and chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature. The topping should be golden and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chives or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef & Root Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Beef & Root Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew is a rich, dark brown, showcasing tender, irregular chunks of seared beef, clearly visible light orange carrot rounds, and creamy white potato chunks. All ingredients are naturally settled within the thick, glossy gravy, with some components gently overlapping. A vibrant sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley sits on top, offering a fresh contrast. The bowl is filled adequately, allowing a portion of its rim to remain visible. The bowl rests on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table, exhibiting its natural grain and subtle imperfections. Beside the bowl, a simple, everyday ceramic plate with a slight chip holds a torn, thick slice of crusty artisanal bread. A casually folded, plain linen napkin in a neutral tone is placed to the side. Warm, inviting lighting, resembling natural light from a kitchen window, casts soft shadows, enhancing the comforting textures of the stew. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a simple kitchen counter, ensuring the focus remains on the inviting meal. A standard metal fork and spoon are positioned next to the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the rich gravy.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 3 medium, peeled, cut into 2 cm thick rounds

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium (e.g., Russet or Yukon Gold), peeled, cut into 3-4 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in tomato paste and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in beef stock and Worcestershire sauce, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add bay leaf.
Add carrots and potatoes to the pot. Ensure vegetables are mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle hot stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For extra richness, add a splash of red wine with the beef stock.
Adjust cooking time based on beef tenderness; it should be fork-tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora con Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Two pieces of braised chicken, one thigh and one drumstick, are nestled among a generous mound of golden tagliatelle. The chicken is deeply browned, almost falling off the bone. The rich, chunky tomato-based sauce, flecked with tender red and green bell pepper strips, quartered mushrooms, and softened onions, generously coats the chicken and pasta. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a pop of color. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, silver fork and a casually placed linen napkin accompany the dish. The lighting is warm and cozy, evoking a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The scene is uncluttered, allowing the robust, comforting dish to be the focal point, reflecting authentic Italian home cooking.
instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Work in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion, red bell pepper strips, green bell pepper strips, and quartered mushrooms to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken pieces to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf sprigs.
While chicken simmers, cook tagliatelle according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
Serve chicken and sauce over the cooked tagliatelle. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of golden-brown roasted chicken and potatoes rests on a rustic ceramic plate. Two crispy-skinned chicken thighs are positioned naturally. Thick-cut potato wedges, roasted to a deep golden hue with soft interiors, are scattered around the chicken. Bright red, blistered cherry tomato halves and softened, light brown roasted garlic cloves are interspersed among the potatoes, adding pops of color and texture. Fresh green rosemary and thyme leaves cling to the roasted ingredients. The arrangement is casual, as if scooped directly from a family pan, filling the plate without overcrowding. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Simple, everyday flatware and a casually folded cloth napkin are nearby. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the comforting, homely atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place chicken thighs, potato wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, and smashed garlic cloves in a large roasting pan.
Add rosemary sprigs and thyme sprigs to the pan.
Drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper.
Toss all ingredients together to coat evenly.
Arrange in a single layer in the roasting pan.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Roasted Potatoes and Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial braised beef short rib, dark and glistening, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its rich, deep brown exterior contrasts with its tender, fall-off-the-bone texture. Around the short rib, a thoughtful arrangement of golden-brown roasted potato wedges shows their crispy skins and fluffy interiors. Scattered among the potatoes are vibrant, burst confit cherry tomatoes, their slightly shriveled skins and bright red pulp adding pops of color. A glossy, reduced red wine and beef jus, infused with caramelized onions, pools elegantly beneath the meat and lightly coats the potatoes. A small sprig of fresh rosemary and a sprinkle of chopped flat-leaf parsley provide a final touch of fresh green. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, with standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, under soft, even natural lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Pat short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs and set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the pot. Add roughly chopped onions and cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is reduced by half.
Return short ribs to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender.

While ribs braise, prepare potatoes and tomatoes. Cut Yukon Gold potatoes into 2.5 cm wedges. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a baking sheet at 200°C for 25-30 minutes, until golden and tender. For tomato confit, toss whole cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast alongside potatoes for the last 15-20 minutes, until burst and slightly shriveled.
Once ribs are cooked, remove them from the pot. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids. Skim any excess fat from the liquid.
Reduce the braising liquid over medium-high heat until it thickens into a glossy sauce. Season with salt and pepper as needed.

To serve, place a single braised short rib on each plate. Arrange roasted potato wedges and confit cherry tomatoes around the rib. Drizzle generously with the reduced braising sauce. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Tenderloin Medallions with Mushroom Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Pork Tenderloin Medallions with Mushroom Cream Sauce. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Three to four golden-brown seared pork medallions, each approximately 2.5 cm thick, are neatly arranged slightly overlapping in the center. A rich, creamy, light brown mushroom sauce, studded with tender, earthy sliced cremini mushrooms, is generously spooned over the pork and pools around its base. The sauce has a velvety texture. A few fresh thyme sprigs are artfully placed on top of the medallions as a vibrant green garnish. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with the deep brown of the seared pork, the lighter brown and cream of the sauce, and the fresh green of the herbs. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery (fork and knife) beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred background typical of a modern bistro.
instructions: Trim pork tenderloin. Remove silver skin. Slice into 2.5 cm thick medallions.
Season pork medallions generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15g butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork medallions 2-3 minutes per side. Brown well. Cook in batches if needed. Do not overcrowd pan.
Remove pork from skillet. Set aside. Keep warm.
Add remaining 15g butter to skillet. Add diced shallots. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms to skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally. Mushrooms should be golden brown.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of pan. Simmer 2 minutes. Reduce slightly.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes. Sauce should thicken slightly.
Return pork medallions to skillet. Include any accumulated juices. Simmer 2-3 minutes. Pork should be cooked through.
Stir in fresh thyme leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Fried Chicken Cutlets with Apple-Mustard Sauce and Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-fried chicken cutlet, perfectly crisp on the exterior and tender within, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous drizzle of creamy, pale yellow apple-mustard sauce cascades over a portion of the chicken and pools delicately beside it. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of golden-roasted potato wedges, their skins slightly crisped and interiors fluffy, are scattered with vibrant green chopped fresh rosemary. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and warm tones of the food. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into 2cm wedges. Roughly chop red onion. Remove rosemary leaves from sprigs. Toss potatoes and red onion with half the olive oil, half the rosemary, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes until tender and golden.
Place each chicken breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound with a mallet until 1.5cm thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, one with panko breadcrumbs. Dredge each chicken cutlet in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing to coat well.

Heat remaining olive oil and butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Pan-fry chicken cutlets for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken, keep warm.

For the sauce, finely dice shallots and apple. In the same pan, add a little more butter if needed. Sauté shallots for 2 minutes until softened. Add diced apple and cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.
Deglaze with white wine if using, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until almost evaporated. Stir in chicken stock, Dijon mustard, and remaining rosemary. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in double cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve each chicken cutlet with a generous portion of roasted potatoes. Spoon apple-mustard sauce over and around the chicken. Garnish with fresh herbs if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Cacciatore presented in a shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs are centered, featuring deeply seared, golden-brown skin glazed with a vibrant red tomato ragu. The sauce is thick and rustic, containing visible chunks of softened yellow onion, earthy-brown halved cremini mushrooms, and blistered red cherry tomatoes. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered loosely over the top. The bowl sits on a dark oak wood table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a small plate of crusty ciabatta bread. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the glossy texture of the sauce and the organic arrangement of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta or focaccia to mop up the sauce.
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti.
Present in a wide shallow bowl to highlight the rustic braise.
instructions: Pat chicken dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion and halved mushrooms to the skillet.
Sauté for 5 minutes until onions are translucent and mushrooms are browned.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Add crushed tomatoes, cherry tomatoes, and chicken stock. Stir to combine.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in fresh torn basil and serve immediately.
notes: Use high-quality canned San Marzano tomatoes for the most authentic flavor profile.
Do not remove the chicken skin, as it provides essential fat and flavor to the braising liquid.
If the sauce is too thick, add a splash more chicken stock at the end.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Savory Oat Risotto and Caramelized Apple
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Savory Oat Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a light wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. The risotto forms a natural, slightly free-flowing mound, showcasing its creamy texture. Three thick, diagonal slices of golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast are arranged naturally on top of the risotto, with no fanning. Beside the chicken, two to three caramelized apple wedges, golden with slightly browned edges, add a warm contrasting color. A sprinkle of fresh green thyme leaves garnishes the dish, providing a pop of color. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the textures and warm tones. A simple cotton napkin and standard flatware rest beside the plate, completing the approachable restaurant-style setup.

ingredients.name: Firm apples (e.g., Honeycrisp, Gala), cored and cut into 8 wedges each

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken, set aside, and let rest 5 minutes. Cover loosely.
In the same skillet, melt 30g butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add steel-cut oats to the skillet. Stir for 2 minutes to toast lightly.

Pour in 100ml chicken broth. Stir until absorbed. Continue adding remaining broth, 100ml at a time, stirring frequently, allowing each addition to be mostly absorbed before adding more. This will take 20-25 minutes. Oats should be creamy and tender but still have a slight bite.

Stir in whole milk and remaining 30g butter. Cook 2-3 minutes until milk is incorporated and risotto is creamy. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep risotto warm.
While risotto cooks, heat 15ml olive oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Add apple wedges. Cook 3-4 minutes per side until tender and lightly caramelized. Drizzle with balsamic glaze if using.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions. Do not fan.

To plate, spoon a generous portion of savory oat risotto onto the center of each plate. Arrange sliced chicken medallions on top of the risotto. Place caramelized apple wedges beside the chicken. Garnish with a few fresh thyme leaves.
notes: For a richer flavor, a splash of dry white wine can be added after toasting the oats and before adding broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Herb Crust, Roasted Potatoes, and Blanched Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast, featuring a golden-brown herb crust, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its crispy texture. To one side, a neat arrangement of roasted potato cubes, approximately 2cm, displays a golden exterior and tender interior. On the opposite side, vibrant green blanched broccoli florets are carefully placed, retaining their crisp-tender texture. A subtle drizzle of glistening pan jus lightly coats parts of the chicken and potatoes. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with appropriate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, bathed in soft, natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes or wedges. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes. Turn halfway, until golden and tender.

Cut broccoli into small florets. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Cook for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately and transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
In a shallow dish, combine panko breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, thyme leaves, minced garlic, 15ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season chicken with salt and pepper on both sides. Press one side of each chicken breast firmly into the breadcrumb mixture to create a crust.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts, breadcrumb-side down, in the hot skillet.
Sear for 3-4 minutes until the crust is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven.
Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. Add remaining 15g butter and chicken stock to the pan. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce liquid slightly to create a light pan jus. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

To plate, arrange roasted potato cubes on one side of each plate. Place blanched broccoli florets on the opposite side. Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast centrally on the plate. Drizzle chicken and potatoes with the pan jus. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Lamb Shank with Root Vegetable Puree and Glazed Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously sized braised lamb shank rests elegantly on a bed of smooth, creamy root vegetable puree. The puree, a pale, inviting orange-yellow, is spread artfully across one side of a round white porcelain plate. Beside the lamb, a small cluster of vibrant orange glazed carrot batons and translucent, tender glazed onion wedges adds a pop of color and texture. A rich, dark red-brown braising liquid is spooned generously over the lamb shank, catching the light. Fresh green parsley leaves are scattered over the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded crisp white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and depth. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere. No other distracting elements are present.
instructions: Pat lamb shanks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear shanks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove shanks. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped large onions, 300g carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce wine by half.
Return lamb shanks to the pot. Add beef or lamb stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Liquid should mostly cover shanks. Add more stock if needed.
Bring to a simmer. Cover tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Braise 2.5-3 hours, or until lamb is fork-tender and falling off the bone.
While lamb braises, prepare root vegetable puree. Peel and chop potatoes and 300g carrots into 2-3 cm chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain well.
Mash potatoes and carrots with 40g butter, salt, and pepper until smooth and creamy. Keep warm.

For glazed carrots: Peel and cut remaining 200g carrots into 4-5 cm batons. Cut small onion into wedges. Melt remaining 10g butter in a small pan over medium heat. Add carrots, onion, sugar, and 50ml water. Cover and cook 8-10 minutes until tender. Uncover and cook until water evaporates and vegetables are lightly glazed.
Once lamb is done, remove shanks from pot. Strain braising liquid into a saucepan. Discard solids. Skim excess fat. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until it thickens into a rich sauce.

Plate: Spoon a generous portion of root vegetable puree onto each plate. Place one lamb shank on top of the puree. Arrange glazed carrot batons and onion wedges beside the lamb. Drizzle reduced braising sauce over the lamb. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Allow lamb shanks to rest for 10 minutes after removing from the oven for optimal tenderness.
Adjust consistency of puree with a splash of warm milk or stock if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Pasta with Seared Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Creamy Tomato Pasta with Seared Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The penne pasta is coated in a vibrant, creamy, reddish-orange tomato sauce, showing its smooth, rich texture. Nestled artfully atop the pasta are several thick, golden-brown seared chicken breast medallions, their edges slightly caramelized, revealing tender white meat. A generous scattering of freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the dish, adding a pale, crumbly texture. Fresh, whole basil leaves, vibrant green, are strategically placed as a garnish, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish maintains moderate negative space, appearing inviting and approachable. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate, with standard silver flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's appealing colors and textures against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the sauce.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1/2 bunch, chopped, plus whole leaves for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove chicken from pan. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Add diced shallots. Cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and 50g grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer 2 minutes.
Add chopped fresh basil. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, until desired consistency.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Divide pasta among four plates. Arrange sliced chicken medallions artfully atop the pasta. Garnish with whole fresh basil leaves and extra grated Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Reserve some pasta cooking water to adjust sauce consistency if needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken Tacos with Fermented Salsa and Pickled Broccoli Stems
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Chicken Tacos is presented on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate, reflecting a natural, minimalist aesthetic. Two warm corn tortillas hold diced, seared chicken cubes, topped with vibrant orange and red fermented bell pepper and carrot salsa. A light scattering of white crumbled Cotija cheese and fresh green cilantro leaves provides contrast. Alongside the tacos, a small mound of tender-crisp, roasted broccoli florets displays shades of deep green, complemented by a few pale green pickled broccoli stem batons. The composition is clean, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, textured bamboo surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural lighting that highlights the ingredients' organic textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, showcasing mindful spacing and unforced arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges for fresh acidity
Offer additional fresh cilantro for garnish
instructions: Prepare Fermented Salsa: Dice red bell pepper and carrot into small cubes. Mince half the red onion and one garlic clove. Combine vegetables in a clean jar. Add 2% salt by weight of vegetables. Cover with water. Seal tightly. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, burping daily, until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.

Prepare Pickled Broccoli Stems: Peel broccoli stems. Cut into 5 cm batons. Blanch in boiling water for 1 minute. Drain. Pack into a clean jar. Heat water and white vinegar to a boil with a pinch of salt. Pour over stems. Seal. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving, or up to 2 weeks.
Prepare Chicken: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. In a bowl, combine chicken with chili powder, cumin, minced remaining garlic, juice of one lime, and a pinch of salt. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Roast Broccoli Florets: Toss broccoli florets with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Roast at 200°C (390°F) for 12-15 minutes, until tender-crisp. Set aside.

Cook Chicken: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken. Cook, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). This takes about 8-10 minutes. Set aside.
Warm Tortillas: Warm corn tortillas on a dry skillet or microwave until pliable.

Assemble Tacos: Place two warm tortillas on each plate. Fill each tortilla with cooked chicken. Top with a spoonful of fermented salsa. Crumble Cotija cheese over the top. Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve with roasted broccoli florets and pickled broccoli stems on the side. Offer lime wedges for squeezing.
notes: This recipe utilizes fermentation and pickling for preservation, reducing food waste and enhancing flavor.
Broccoli stems, often discarded, are repurposed into a delicious pickled accompaniment.
The recipe focuses on seasonal vegetables and plant-forward elements, with chicken as a complementary protein.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Umami Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sustainable Umami Noodle Soup is presented in a handcrafted, natural ceramic bowl with an organic, matte finish in cream or beige. The rich, clear amber broth forms the base. Visible are tender chunks of slow-cooked beef, generous portions of shredded chicken, and al dente whole wheat fusilli. Thinly sliced leek rounds and earthy mushroom slices are naturally scattered within the broth. The dish is garnished simply with a few vibrant green parsley leaves and a delicate, thinly sliced radish. The composition is clean and minimalistic, allowing each ingredient to stand out. The bowl sits on a light, reclaimed wood table surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, with a hint of green from a background plant, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Whole wheat fusilli or penne pasta
Onion peels, carrot tops, celery ends, mushroom stems (vegetable scraps)
Leek (white and green parts), thinly sliced
Fresh parsley or dill, for garnish
Crispy kale stems or radish slices, for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast beef bones and chicken carcass on a baking sheet for 30 minutes until browned.
Transfer roasted bones and carcass to a large stock pot. Add vegetable scraps, crushed garlic, and ginger. Cover with 3 L cold water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 4-6 hours. Skim any foam. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.

Season the strained broth with salt and pepper. Add beef chuck to the broth. Simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until very tender. Remove beef, let cool slightly, then shred or cut into 2-3 cm chunks. Set aside.
Add chicken thighs to the simmering broth. Poach for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, let cool, then shred. Set aside.
In a separate pot, cook whole wheat fusilli according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Return broth to a simmer. Stir in fermented tomato paste. Add sliced leek and mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
To serve, divide cooked pasta among four bowls. Ladle hot broth with leeks and mushrooms over pasta. Arrange shredded beef and chicken chunks on top.
Garnish each bowl with fresh parsley or dill, and crispy kale stems or radish slices if using. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing vegetable scraps and bones for a flavorful broth.
Fermented tomato paste adds depth of flavor and aligns with sustainable food practices.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken with Mayonnaise and Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of baked chicken with mayonnaise and cheese is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate with a subtle blue floral pattern, typical of Russian home dinnerware. The chicken breast cutlet, a whole, thick piece, is generously topped with a rich layer of caramelized golden-brown sautéed onion rings, beneath a thick, bubbly, melted cheese crust. The cheese is slightly browned at the edges, revealing hints of creamy mayonnaise beneath. A small sprig of fresh dill or parsley is casually placed on the melted cheese. The plate rests slightly off-center on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple silver fork and knife are positioned to the side of the plate. In the softly blurred background, a slice of dark rye bread and a small bowl of pickled cucumbers hint at a traditional Russian family meal, all bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a side of boiled potatoes, mashed potatoes, or buckwheat kasha (grechka).
Often accompanied by simple fresh vegetable salads or pickled vegetables.
Rye bread is a common accompaniment at the Russian table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Slice chicken breasts horizontally into 2 cm thick cutlets. Lightly pound each cutlet to an even thickness.
Season chicken cutlets on both sides with salt and black pepper.
Thinly slice onions into rings. Mince garlic.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sliced onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the onions. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant. Remove from heat.
Grate the hard cheese.
Arrange seasoned chicken cutlets in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Spread a generous layer of sautéed onions and garlic evenly over each chicken cutlet.
Top the onion layer with a spoonful of mayonnaise, spreading it to cover the onions.
Sprinkle a thick layer of grated cheese over the mayonnaise on each cutlet.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and cheese is golden brown and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh dill or parsley if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C for food safety.
Do not overcook the chicken to keep it moist and tender.
Adjust mayonnaise quantity based on preference for creaminess.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom and Thyme Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, its golden-brown, crispy skin glistening, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, creamy mushroom and thyme sauce, studded with earthy-toned sliced mushrooms, pools generously beside and slightly over the chicken. A neat, fluffy mound of herbed brown rice, flecked with bright green chopped parsley, sits adjacent to the chicken. The composition is balanced and inviting, showcasing natural ingredient colors and inviting textures. A fresh thyme sprig garnishes the chicken, adding a vibrant green accent. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with standard silverware and a folded cotton napkin beside it, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro-style background, highlighting the dish as the main subject.

ingredients.name: Mixed mushrooms (e.g., cremini, shiitake, oyster), cleaned and sliced

instructions: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions. Typically, combine 250g rice with 500ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped parsley.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear for 2-3 minutes on the second side.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet; set aside on a plate, tented with foil.
Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. Add butter. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add shallots and garlic. Cook for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until liquid is almost evaporated. Add chicken stock and 2 thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Remove thyme sprigs.

To serve, place a portion of herbed brown rice on each plate. Arrange one chicken breast next to the rice. Spoon generous amounts of creamy mushroom sauce over and around the chicken. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot Couscous Salad with Quick-Pickled Chickpeas
recipes.visual_description: Couscous salad arranged naturally on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone (cream or beige). Small, uniformly diced carrots, cucumber, and red bell pepper are visible throughout the fluffy couscous. Quick-pickled chickpeas add pops of pale yellow. A vibrant green drizzle of carrot top pesto is artfully swirled on top, with flecks of fresh herbs. The presentation is clean and unfussy, highlighting the natural colors and textures. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly beside it. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish. The background is minimalist, with a subtle hint of green from a nearby plant. An individual serving, with ingredients thoughtfully distributed to showcase variety and freshness.

ingredients.name: Carrot tops (from 2 carrots), washed and dried

instructions: Place couscous in a bowl. Bring broth or water to a boil. Pour over couscous. Cover and let sit for 5-7 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.

For quick-pickled chickpeas: In a small pot, combine 120ml water, apple cider vinegar, 1 tsp salt, and optional sugar. Bring to a simmer until salt dissolves. Pour hot brine over rinsed chickpeas in a heatproof jar. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

For carrot top pesto: In a food processor, combine carrot tops, parsley, minced garlic, 50ml olive oil, and lemon juice. Pulse until a coarse pesto forms. Season with salt and pepper. Add a splash more olive oil if too thick.
Dice carrots, cucumber, and red bell pepper into small, uniform pieces.
In a large bowl, combine fluffed couscous, diced carrots, cucumber, and red bell pepper. Add quick-pickled chickpeas, draining most of the brine.
Spoon a generous amount of carrot top pesto over the salad. Toss gently to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately or chill.
notes: For deeper fermentation, combine cooked chickpeas with a 2% brine (20g salt per 1 liter water) and ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days.
Any leftover pesto can be stored in the fridge or frozen in ice cube trays for future use.
Adjust vegetables based on seasonal availability: blanched green beans, roasted sweet potato cubes, or chopped kale are good additions.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken, Potato, and Bell Pepper Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Chicken, Potato, and Bell Pepper Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is positioned prominently on top of a generous bed of vibrant, moist rice. The rice is studded with diced red and green bell peppers, soft pieces of red onion, small tender cubes of potato, and hints of red from the crushed tomatoes, creating a rich mosaic of colors and textures. Freshly chopped green basil leaves are scattered over the dish, providing a pop of fresh color and aromatic contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a delicate white layer on top. The dish has a natural, flowing arrangement, avoiding rigid shapes. The background features a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded white cotton napkin, and a subtle, casual restaurant ambiance with natural, even lighting. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space around the food.

ingredients.name: Fresh red chili
ingredients.quantity: 1, finely minced (seeds removed for less heat)

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium (approx. 200g), peeled and diced into 1cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear for another 3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced red onion, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, and minced chili to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, Arborio rice, and diced potato to the skillet. Stir for 2 minutes until rice is translucent.
Pour in the beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Cook until beer is almost fully absorbed.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the skillet tightly with a lid or foil. Transfer to the preheated oven. Bake for 25 minutes.
Remove from oven. Stir the rice and potato gently. If needed, add a splash more broth if mixture seems too dry. Sprinkle half of the fresh basil and half of the grated Parmesan over the dish.

Return to oven, uncovered, and bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C), rice is tender, and potatoes are soft. Liquid should be mostly absorbed but dish should still be moist.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan.
notes: The provided ingredients (chicken, tomato, onion, chili, parmesan, bell pepper, basil, beer, rice, potato) are savory and not suitable for a sweet cake. This recipe has been designed as a savory baked chicken and rice dish to best utilize the given ingredients while adhering to the 'casual dining' and 'simple restaurant style' presentation requirements.

recipes.recipe_name: Brined Pork Loin with Tomato-Onion Confit and Quick Pickled Red Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick-cut piece of seared pork loin, displaying a golden-brown crust and a tender, slightly pink interior, is placed off-center on a round, cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate. Beside the pork, a generous mound of slow-roasted tomato and onion confit showcases rich, ruby-red tomato halves and soft, golden-brown caramelized onion slices. A vibrant scattering of thinly sliced, pale pink quick pickled red onions adds a contrasting pop of color and texture. Roasted root vegetables, such as golden parsnip wedges and deep orange carrot chunks, are artfully arranged to one side, showing their natural char. The dish is subtly garnished with a few fresh parsley leaves. The plate sits on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded neatly beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, and the background is clean and minimalist.
instructions: Prepare brine: Dissolve 100g salt in 2 litres cold water. Submerge pork loin in brine. Refrigerate for 2-4 hours.

Prepare quick pickled red onions: Thinly slice red onions. In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, 100ml water, sugar, peppercorns, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Pour hot liquid over sliced red onions in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

Prepare tomato-onion confit: Preheat oven to 160°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice brown onions. Mince garlic. In a roasting dish, combine tomatoes, brown onions, minced garlic, 50ml olive oil, and thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 45-60 minutes, or until vegetables are very tender and slightly caramelized.

Prepare roasted root vegetables: Peel and chop root vegetables into 2cm chunks. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast in oven with confit for 30-40 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.

Cook pork: Remove pork from brine. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. Discard brine. Heat remaining 20ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove from oven, transfer pork to a cutting board. Rest for 10 minutes.

Assemble: Slice pork loin into 2cm thick pieces. Arrange pork on individual plates. Spoon generous portions of tomato-onion confit alongside. Add roasted root vegetables. Garnish with quick pickled red onions and fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan-Style Pasta with Roasted Tomatoes and Cannellini Beans
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, featuring a generous, artfully mounded portion of rigatoni pasta. The pasta, cooked al dente, is coated in a rich, rustic tomato and cannellini bean sauce. Bursting, deeply colored roasted cherry tomatoes are visibly interspersed throughout the pasta, alongside tender, creamy cannellini beans. Vibrant green, wilted spinach leaves provide a fresh contrast, integrated seamlessly. The texture is inviting, with the sauce clinging well to the pasta. A garnish of fresh, whole basil leaves is scattered over the top, along with a light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a neatly folded cotton napkin, all illuminated by natural, even lighting for a professional yet approachable bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
A simple green salad with a lemon vinaigrette can accompany it.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese or Pecorino Romano at the table for individual preference.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans
ingredients.quantity: 2 x 400 g cans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
While tomatoes roast, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat remaining 45 ml olive oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. This is the soffritto base.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and cannellini beans. Add vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Stir well to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Gently fold in roasted cherry tomatoes and fresh spinach. Cook for 2-3 minutes until spinach wilts.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure pasta is cooked al dente for optimal texture.
Roasting the cherry tomatoes deepens their flavor and adds a smoky sweetness to the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Simplified Hainanese Chicken Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Simplified Hainanese Chicken Rice is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The centerpiece is tender, poached chicken, cut into thick, rustic chunks, with its glistening skin intact. The chicken is arranged casually on one side of the plate, not fanned.
